svg.text: java 21 · spring boot 3.5 · react 19 · postgresql 16 · bachelor thesis
Small businesses run on processes nobody ever wrote down, and when someone leaves the process
leaves with them. Existing process-mining tools want an event log a twelve-person studio does
not have. FlowOps starts from what exists: somebody taps a circle beside a chat message, and
Dependency rules enforced by ArchUnit in CI. 91 tables over 104 forward-only migrations.
Invariants held by partial unique indexes rather than service-layer checks. Every endpoint
round-tripped against a real PostgreSQL in Testcontainers.
The constraint I am most pleased with: does this help a business run a process it already
performs, without ever producing a number about a person? A per-person productivity score clears
every technical review and fails that sentence.
